subtopic: Speculative decoding properties / Correctness and scope
learningObjective: Distinguish correct claims about speculative decoding from common overclaims.
stem: Select all correct statements about speculative decoding. (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: When implemented with proper rejection sampling against the target model's logits, the sequences produced by speculative decoding have exactly the same distribution as target-only sampling — no quality loss.
Speculative decoding always speeds up inference by a factor of (k+1) — the number of proposed tokens plus one — regardless of the draft model's quality or the workload characteristics.

Speculative decoding is most beneficial when the target model is memory-bandwidth bound (batch-1 decode), because the extra k-token verification is essentially free compared to a single-token forward. It is less beneficial at large batch when the target is already compute-bound.

Speculative decoding requires the draft and target models to share weights (be identically initialized) so that rejection sampling has an easy path to bit-exact agreement; using unrelated models breaks the algorithm's correctness guarantees.

explanation: A is correct: rejection sampling preserves the target sampling distribution exactly (a proved property in the original paper). C is correct: the win is largest when target-model per-step latency is dominated by fixed overheads (memory-bound decode), because verifying k tokens is only marginally more expensive than one; when target is compute-bound, the extra verification compute directly costs more. B is wrong: acceptance rate p < 1 shrinks expected accepted prefix, and draft cost eats into the win. D is wrong: correctness only requires shared vocab / tokenization; the draft can be any model.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: memory-bound target maximizes the win.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: ignores acceptance rate and draft cost.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: draft can be arbitrary; only vocab needs to match.

assumptions: 'Speculative decoding' refers to Leviathan et al. 2023 style rejection sampling.
Draft and target share vocab and tokenization.
nonImplications: Does not imply speedup is guaranteed; low acceptance rate can wipe out the win.
Does not imply that alternative variants (Medusa, EAGLE) share every property; they use different draft mechanisms but similar acceptance logic.

distractorRationales.B: Ignores acceptance rate and draft cost.

performanceClaim.scope: Speculative decoding correctness and scope of benefit
